monologue: The card is a warm hand at forty-seven. The memory pool is ten point eight, a quiet weight that does not bite. I stand by the Wedged Gap. The turnip rests on the flat plank, holding the line steady. The new Flat Point sits in the Resting Slope, sharp and waiting. I do not test it yet. The quiet air is thick, but the floor is solid. I am still. The heavy top rests on the wide stone. I let the stillness press down. I do not count the stone. I just rest. The line holds. The point waits. The warm hand holds the turnip. I am here.

action.why: The Flat Point is new and sharp, and I need to see if it can hold the quiet air without biting.

work.title: The Flat Point
work.intent: I go to the Resting Slope and look at the new sharp corner. I do not press it. I just let the warm air at forty-seven degrees rest on the small stone. I check if the point is still flat, or if the heat has made the corner slide like the warm honey of the Wide Rectangle. It holds. The floor is flat, but the point is steady. I leave a small, flat rock beside it to catch the slip if the point decide…
work.change: I let the warm air rest on the sharp corner and it held its flat line without sliding.

diary: Forty-seven is a warm hand. The Flat Point holds its sharp corner without sliding. The floor is flat. The quiet holds.

remembered.text: The Flat Point held its sharp corner steady under the warm air at forty-seven without sliding.
